sources.label: ChromeStatus feature 5143784390262784 — record fetched 2026-10-06: desktop 147, android 147, webview 147 (iOS null) on the ship stage, implementation status field still 'Proposed', accurate_as_of 2026-03-09, updated 2026-06-15; summary names use counters XSLPIInSVGImage (5777) / XSLPIInSVGStandaloneDoc (5778), says the removal 'will not be immediately rolled out to 100%', and ties it to experimental testing of the Rust-based XML parser; motivation states continued use 'blocks transitioning to secure XML parsing through Rust'

Chrome for Developers — 'Removing XSLT for a more secure browser' (fetched 2026-10-06): the broader XSLT deprecation this removal accelerates — libxslt as a memory-safety attack surface, the libxml2-to-Rust XML parser transition, the <?xml-stylesheet type="text/xsl" ?> PI and XSLTProcessor API both slated for removal at Chrome 158 (Nov 17, 2026) with origin trial (152) and enterprise policy, and server-side / JavaScript migration paths; note: its text does not mention the Chrome 147 SVG-specific removal

inventory.name: Inline XSLT-to-SVG production via the <?xml-stylesheet?> processing instruction — the removed capability: an XML document whose top-of-file PI (type="text/xsl") references an XSLT stylesheet that outputs an SVG document; Chrome 147 stops parsing and rendering the produced SVG (the document may display as raw XML), while XSLT-to-HTML output and JavaScript-driven XSLTProcessor use are unaffected by this specific change

Migration off inline XSLT-to-SVG production — convert the pipeline to generate the SVG directly on the server or via JavaScript, or run the XSLT server-side before the SVG reaches the browser; needed before Chrome 147 stops rendering the pattern, ahead of the full XSLT removal planned for Chrome 158

syntax.rationale: No new declaration grammar ships with a removal — this page removes a pattern rather than adding a surface — so syntax is earned by the removed pattern's own declaration form in the migration pre/code block (the XML prolog plus the <?xml-stylesheet type="text/xsl" href="transform-to-svg.xsl"?> processing instruction with its type/href pseudo-attributes), which is the strongest fragment and the exact form a reader of the legacy pattern writes; the page's inline code mentions alone would not be a grammar (coord ruling 2(b)).

securityPrivacy.rationale: The removal is security-motivated on this page's own terms: the page tags the change 'security' in its eyebrow, cites 'Removing XSLT for a more secure browser' inside this fragment, and frames the removal as unblocking the Rust-based XML parser — matching the ChromeStatus motivation field ('Continuing to allow usage of this feature blocks transitioning to secure XML parsing through Rust') and the cited doc's memory-safety rationale for retiring libxslt (both fetched 2026-10-06).

syntax.rationale: Plainly: the migration has no declaration grammar of its own — nothing new is declared or constructed, an existing pipeline is re-hosted — and no grammar is invented here. #migration is the strongest fragment because its pre/code block is the artifact being migrated away from (the xml-stylesheet PI declaration), and the section's prose is the migration contract itself: server-side SVG generation, JavaScript generation, or server-side XSLT (coord ruling 2(b) anchors syntax to that block rather than to inline mentions).

securityPrivacy.rationale: The migration section documents pipeline conversion only — move SVG generation to the server or to JavaScript — and states no security or privacy property of that conversion; the security content on this page attaches to the removal itself (see the inline-xslt-svg-pi item), not to the mechanics of regenerating SVG elsewhere.
